_comment: Spatial words drawn as a picture, not searched for and not clozed (tunatale-hvj0, the user 2026-09-28: 'they become picture cards'). Each maps a word to a language-neutral concept in app.cards.spatial_scenes.SPATIAL_CONCEPTS. A word listed here is NOT a function word, whatever `function_words.json` or a POS tag says: app.srs.function_words.is_function_word vetoes it, so it cards as vocab and its image is drawn. The picture is only drawn when the card's English gloss names the relation (app.cards.spatial_picture.gloss_matches), which is what keeps a homograph's other sense off the picture. Map only words whose MAIN sense is spatial: the case marker 'sa' stays a cloze. 'wala' (none / left), 'tuo' (right / believe) and 'tunga' (half / middle) are homographs: they are listed, and the gloss guard draws them only on a card glossed with the spatial sense. ORCHESTRATOR-DRAFTED, not native-checked. Distinct words get distinct pictures (2026-09-29, tunatale-fsyd): kilid ('side') no longer shares tupad's beside, and tunga ('middle') no longer shares taliwala's between; both are parts of the box, like top and bottom. 2026-10-14: gikan (from) and padulong (toward) added, drawn with a flag for the place; the user chose the flag over a house. 2026-10-14 (tunatale-qas4): the four distances from the people talking, after Wolff: kini 'this (near speaker and person spoken to)', kiri 'near speaker but not near hearer', kana 'near hearer', kadto 'far from speaker and hearer', and dinhi / diri / diha / didto for places. Wolff has no diri headword; it follows ari ('here, near speaker but not near person spoken to') the way dinhi follows anhi. The user kept all four distances. 2026-10-18 (the user: 'Nia also seems like a good svg candidate'): being there, the existential. Wolff: nía = anía 'is here, where you and I are' (Wolff 1: 'Nia man', he is here); túa = atúa 'is there, far away'. Drawn as a lit person at that distance, which is neither the thing (ball) nor the place (flag). 2026-10-22 (the user: 'Share the drawing'): the long forms ania and atua share their short forms' pictures, a recorded synonym exception in test_spatial_picture.py. Same day ('Draw near-you'): naa = anaa, Wolff anáa {1} 'be there (near you)' {2} 'there is' {3} 'has', is drawn as someone at your distance; the user chose it over keeping the photo, knowing the general 'there is' is the commoner sense. The gloss guard keeps the 'has' sense off it. 2026-10-27 (tunatale-tofg.5): the rest of Wolff Beginning Cebuano's §1A demonstrative charts, with time (was / will be) and the genitive (of this / of that), drawn as the owner chose from the mockups: the past and future are an outline person at that distance with an arrow and a tether, the genitive is the thing with a bag beside it. A word may list several concepts in priority order (diri = was here, or here; adto = will be there, or of that); the gloss picks the sense, and a word whose gloss names none is left on its route.
